title: Generating and Plotting Synthetic 1D Linear Regression Data
description: Sample uniform features X in [0, 2), compute a linear target using the supplied slope and intercept, and add Gaussian noise. Scatter-plot (X[:, 0], y).
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: Set `n` to the supplied sample count and draw a 2D feature column `X = 2 * np.random.rand(n, 1)` on `[0, 2)`. Compute the noiseless linear values `y_true = theta1_true * X[:, 0] + theta0_true`.
Draw zero-mean Gaussian noise with `np.random.randn(n)` scaled by the supplied standard deviation. Add it to `y_true` to produce the observed 1D target array `y`.

Look at how `X` and `y` are constructed: `X` has one column and a row for each sample. `X[:, 0]` slices column 0 as a 1D vector. Thus, `y_true + noise` produces a 1D target vector with one entry per sample.

steps.question: What are the true intercept and true slope of `y_true` on lines 5-7? What vertical spread around `y_true` does the supplied Gaussian noise introduce?
steps.answer: The true intercept is `theta0_true`, and the true slope is `theta1_true`. Zero-mean Gaussian noise with the supplied standard deviation is added to each point.

steps.description: Call `plt.scatter` on `X[:, 0]` and `y` with the supplied opacity and label `"data"`. Set axis labels `"x"` and `"y"` and the plot title, add the legend, and render with `plt.show()`.
